chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Martha Raye, Sleepy and Lincoln: pianists of Kansas City
summary: Martha Raye stayed two weeks. She recalls Sleepy, who played like Art Tatum in the hard keys, and Lincoln, the only pianist Martha would sing with.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Someone told me her age while she was there, but she was getting well known among musicians because she could really sing and she got herself a movie. The strange thing about it, with all the great pianists around including Sleepy - you know he's the type of pianist that played like Art Tatum in B natural and A natural, exactly like him.
But only in B natural and A natural?
That's right, in all the hard keys.
Did Sleepy have any other name?
No, I don't remember it. That's all we ever called him. I met him in Kansas City 2 or 3 weeks ago; he's still around.

Yes, yes. There was another pianist that had a terrific beat. His name was Lincoln and I'm telling you he could really swing. That's the only pianist that Martha would sing with. She'd grab Lincoln and they'd start singing and then Joe Turner would sing and they had some great sessions there.
This was the time when Martha was supposed to go to Hollywood and she wouldn't leave?
Yes, she wouldn't leave. She stayed about 2 weeks. She was supposed to just drop off and change trains in Kansas City but she heard about Piney Brown's place and she wanted to see it.
Oh, I see, this was the first time she had ever been there?
It was the first time she'd ever been to Kansas City.
I don't know, because I left maybe 3 or 4 years after that. But what a time she had.
